# Why the Market's Surging Despite the Headlines

First listed: 2025-07-14 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Why the Market's Surging Despite the Headlines](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OylH8Sk3SPg) - 2025-07-14
- [Substack: Why the Market's Surging Despite the Headlines](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/why-the-markets-surging-despite-the-ced) - 2025-07-14

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Chris Verrone argues that broad participation, subdued sentiment and cyclical leadership support further gains after the April rebound. His six- and twelve-month S&P direction proved right, while his H2 gold reversal failed. Eisman retains tariff concerns, advances a regional-bank consolidation thesis and explains AI demand for power and cooling. He raises software-moat risks and distinguishes Bitcoin profits from proof of a hedge thesis. The episode rewards separating signal, mechanism and outcome: successful index forecasts do not validate every chart narrative or transfer guest calls to Eisman.

Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.

## Framework and tools

- Compare market breadth and sentiment with capitalization-weighted indexes.
- Use historical conditional patterns while acknowledging small samples and exceptions.
- Separate economic forecasts from asset-return forecasts.
- Map AI demand into physical infrastructure and incumbent software competition.
- A correct security return does not prove the proposed causal story.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- S&P stocks above 50-day moving average
- New-high counts and advance-decline line
- Put/call ratios, investor surveys and fund flows
- 65-trading-day rebound comparisons
- Sector-neutral momentum
- Credit spreads
- Cyclicals/defensives and discretionary/energy ratios
- Goldman/Apollo relative chart
- Gold versus 200-day moving average
- US and foreign sovereign yields

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews Chris Verrone. Explicit agreement and separate host theses are captured individually. Short acknowledgments and requests for explanation are not treated as adoption of every guest target.
- Recorded July 7, 2025, published July 14; both dates matter for returns.
- Eisman says February 29 although 2025 has no such date; the guest supplies February 19.
- Chart images are not in the text; proprietary breadth and backtests were not independently reconstructed.
- The historical drawdown threshold is explicitly relaxed from 15% to 5% to expand the sample.
- Verrone immediately mentions Mitsubishi after Eisman’s two-supplier gas-turbine claim.
- Guest gold, dollar and foreign-equity calls are not automatically Eisman endorsements.
